before.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]). Let a **matter sector** be
specified as follows: a finite list of tensor fields $\psi$ on a spacetime
carrying $\Sigma$, a smooth stress-energy construction $T(g,\psi)$ and a system
of equations $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that, in every chart, the combined system for
$(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] clause (b) attached is a first-order
quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms
in the first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on-shell. Suppose smooth initial data $\psi_0$ on
$\Sigma$ are given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
hold on $\Sigma$ for the normal vector $n$ and the stress tensor determined by
$(h,K,\psi_0)$ ([[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]). Then:

**(a)** every $p\in\Sigma$ has an open neighborhood $O_p$ in $\Sigma$ such that
there are an open neighborhood $W_p$ of $O_p$ in a smooth four-manifold, a smooth
Lorentzian metric $g$ and matter fields $\psi$ on $W_p$ solving the field
equations $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T(g,\psi)$ and the matter equations, with
$O_p$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface of induced metric $h$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the local solutions of (a) glue: over a neighborhood $W$ of $\Sigma$
there are $g,\psi$ solving the equations, with $\Sigma$ spacelike of data
$(h,K)$, and $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its domain of dependence in $W$,
so that $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is an open globally hyperbolic neighborhood of
$\Sigma$ with $\Sigma$ as a Cauchy hypersurface and $(g,\psi)$ restricts to a
globally hyperbolic development of the data;

**(c)** any two developments as in (a)--(b) of the same data are related near
$\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry
([[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]]).

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold carrying a chart $(x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ whose
domain $U$ contains the slice $\Sigma:=\{t=0\}$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth
background metric on $U$ with its Levi--Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $U$ together with the
background-covariant derivatives needed below (the matter field data). Suppose
smooth functions $g^0_{ab},g^1_{ab}$ on $\Sigma\cap U$ are given such that:

1. $g^0_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth Lorentzian metric on
   $\Sigma\cap U$ with $g^{00}_0<0$ and positive definite spatial block
   $(g_0^{ij})$;
2. $g^1_{ab}$ is symmetric and agrees on $\Sigma$ with the components of
   $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ for some smooth extension $g$ of $g^0$ to $U$;
3. the harmonic-gauge condition $H^a=0$ holds on $\Sigma\cap U$ for the pair
   $(g,\bar g)$ ([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]).

Then there is an open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma\cap U$ and a smooth
metric $g$ on $V$ with $g|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^0$ and
$\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^1_{ab}$, solving the **reduced Einstein
equation** with the given background $\bar g$ and matter tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]) on $V$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal
$n$, induced metric $h$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$G$ and $S$ be the Einstein tensor and scalar curvature of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then, at every $p\in\Sigma$
and for all tangential vectors $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z);$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g\bigl(R^g(X,Y)Z,n\bigr)=(\nabla^h_XK)(Y,Z)-(\nabla^h_YK)(X,Z);$$

**(c) normal projections.**
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12\bigl(S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2\bigr),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK);$$

**(d) constraint equations.** If in addition the field equation
$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$ for a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ and
constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
for every tangential $Y$.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$, and
let $\mathcal D$ be fixed smooth initial data for a symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ on
$\Sigma$ (its value and the value of its normal derivative in the models below).
Let $(M,g,N)$ and $(M',g',N')$ be two time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds with spacelike embeddings $j,j'$ of $\Sigma$ inducing the
same $(h,K)$, carrying smooth symmetric tensors $T,T'$ satisfying the field
equations
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G'_{ab}+\Lambda g'_{ab}=\kappa T'_{ab}$$
on neighborhoods of the images of $\Sigma$, with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$,
$\nabla'^aT'_{ab}=0$ there and with equal initial data $\mathcal D$ for
$T,T'$ (transported by the embeddings).

Then there are open neighborhoods $U$ of $j(\Sigma)$ and $U'$ of
$j'(\Sigma)$ and a smooth diffeomorphism $\varphi:U\to U'$ such that:

1. $\varphi(j(\sigma))=j'(\sigma)$ for every $\sigma\in\Sigma$;
2. $\varphi^*(g')=g$ and $\varphi^*(T')=T$ on $U$;
3. $\varphi$ carries the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$.

Thus any two solutions of the field equation arising from the same constrained
geometric data are locally isometric near the initial surface by a
data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry. Here an **isometry fixing the
data** means a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying (2) (the definition is given
explicitly by these equations; no separate notion of Lorentzian isometry is
presupposed).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open
interval with $0\in I$ and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open ball centred
at $0$ of radius $R>0$ with a fixed Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose
$(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$
onto $I\times B$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) such
that, writing $v^s:=ds(v)$ and $v^\sigma:=d\sigma(v)$ for $v\in T_qM$,
$q\in U$:

**(C1)** $\partial/\partial s$ is future timelike and every level set
$s^{-1}(c)$ is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that every future causal $v\in T_qM$, $q\in U$,
satisfies $|v^\sigma|\le K\,v^s$.

On the open submanifold $U$ with the induced metric and time orientation
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]), let
$$D^\pm_U(S):=\bigl\{p\in U:\ \text{every past- (respectively future-) inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\bigr\}$$
be the domains of dependence of the spacelike slice
$S:=s^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\times B$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (d), computed in
$U$. Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$;

**(b)** the open set $Q:=\{q\in U:|s(q)|+K\,|\sigma(q)|<R\}$ is contained in
$D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely
$Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$, and $Q$
is a neighbourhood of $S$ in $U$;

**(c)** the open set $W:=\mathrm{int}_U\bigl(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)\bigr)$
satisfies $Q\subseteq W$, and $S$ is a Cauchy set of the open submanifold
$(W,g|_W)$: every causal curve in $W$ that is inextendible in $W$ meets $S$
in exactly one parameter value. Consequently, $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$ is globally
hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Let $M^m$ be a smooth manifold, let $k\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $0\le k\le m$,
and let $S\subseteq M$. One says that $S$ is an **embedded $k$-dimensional
submanifold** of $M$ when for every $p\in S$ there
is a smooth chart $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with $p\in U$
such that

$$\varphi(S\cap U)=\varphi(U)\cap(\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}).$$

Such a chart is a **slice chart** for $S$ at $p$. The topology on $S$ is the
subspace topology inherited from $M$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

The next lemma proves that the restricted slice charts define a smooth
$k$-manifold structure on $S$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

derivations.claim: (Local existence (a).) Fix $p\in\Sigma$ and a coordinate ball $O_p$ around $p$ small enough that a normal-coordinate product neighborhood of $O_p$ exists. By [L1] build the harmonic initial data for the metric variables on $O_p$, and extend the matter data $\psi_0$ to a smooth germ with the prescribed normal derivative; by [L2] the reduced system coupled to the matter reduction has a smooth solution on a product neighborhood of $O_p$; the gauge vector and the constraint residuals vanish on $O_p$, so by [L2] the solution satisfies the field equation and the matter equations there, and by construction the induced metric and second fundamental form of $O_p$ are $(h,K)$. This gives (a).

(Gluing (b), first part). For two coordinate balls $O_1,O_2$ with nonempty overlap, restrict both solutions to the overlap; both have induced data $(h,K)$ and satisfy the field and matter equations, so by [L3] there is a data-fixing isometry between neighborhoods of the overlap; in particular the metric and matter fields agree after applying the isometry, and since the isometry fixes the surface pointwise on the overlap it is the identity there; hence the two local solutions coincide on the overlap. Therefore the local solutions glue to a smooth solution $(g,\psi)$ on a neighborhood $W$ of $\Sigma$ with the stated properties.

(The surface is Cauchy on its domain of dependence (b), second part). Shrink $W$ to a product neighborhood $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times\Sigma$ of the normal coordinate $s$ in which the level sets of $s$ are spacelike. At $s=0$, $\Sigma$ is acausal (a causal curve from a point of $\Sigma$ to a different point of $\Sigma$ would have a nonpositive tangent at an interior minimum of $s$, contradicting its causal character). In a conically bounded product chart, [L4] gives local Cauchy neighborhoods around each point of $\Sigma$; since every inextendible causal curve through a nearby point enters the local cone region and meets the base patch, the domain of dependence of $\Sigma$ contains the open sets $\{|s|<\epsilon_p,\ d(x,\Sigma\text{-point})<\lambda(\epsilon_p-|s|)\}$ over finitely many charts covering a compact piece; hence every point of $\Sigma$ is interior to $D(\Sigma)\cap W$, and $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is open. Every inextendible causal curve in $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ meets $\Sigma$ exactly once by the definition of the domain of dependence and acausality, so $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy hypersurface for that open neighborhood; by [L4] $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is then globally hyperbolic with compact causal diamonds.

$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold carrying a chart $(x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ whose
domain $U$ contains the slice $\Sigma:=\{t=0\}$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth
background metric on $U$ with its Levi--Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $U$ together with the
background-covariant derivatives needed below (the matter field data). Suppose
smooth functions $g^0_{ab},g^1_{ab}$ on $\Sigma\cap U$ are given such that:

1. $g^0_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth Lorentzian metric on
   $\Sigma\cap U$ with $g^{00}_0<0$ and positive definite spatial block
   $(g_0^{ij})$;
2. $g^1_{ab}$ is symmetric and agrees on $\Sigma$ with the components of
   $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ for some smooth extension $g$ of $g^0$ to $U$;
3. the harmonic-gauge condition $H^a=0$ holds on $\Sigma\cap U$ for the pair
   $(g,\bar g)$ ([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]).

Then there is an open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma\cap U$ and a smooth
metric $g$ on $V$ with $g|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^0$ and
$\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^1_{ab}$, solving the **reduced Einstein
equation** with the given background $\bar g$ and matter tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]) on $V$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal
$n$, induced metric $h$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$G$ and $S$ be the Einstein tensor and scalar curvature of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then, at every $p\in\Sigma$
and for all tangential vectors $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z);$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g\bigl(R^g(X,Y)Z,n\bigr)=(\nabla^h_XK)(Y,Z)-(\nabla^h_YK)(X,Z);$$

**(c) normal projections.**
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12\bigl(S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2\bigr),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK);$$

**(d) constraint equations.** If in addition the field equation
$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$ for a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ and
constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
for every tangential $Y$.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$, and
let $\mathcal D$ be fixed smooth initial data for a symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ on
$\Sigma$ (its value and the value of its normal derivative in the models below).
Let $(M,g,N)$ and $(M',g',N')$ be two time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds with spacelike embeddings $j,j'$ of $\Sigma$ inducing the
same $(h,K)$, carrying smooth symmetric tensors $T,T'$ satisfying the field
equations
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G'_{ab}+\Lambda g'_{ab}=\kappa T'_{ab}$$
on neighborhoods of the images of $\Sigma$, with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$,
$\nabla'^aT'_{ab}=0$ there and with equal initial data $\mathcal D$ for
$T,T'$ (transported by the embeddings).

Then there are open neighborhoods $U$ of $j(\Sigma)$ and $U'$ of
$j'(\Sigma)$ and a smooth diffeomorphism $\varphi:U\to U'$ such that:

1. $\varphi(j(\sigma))=j'(\sigma)$ for every $\sigma\in\Sigma$;
2. $\varphi^*(g')=g$ and $\varphi^*(T')=T$ on $U$;
3. $\varphi$ carries the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$.

geometric data are locally isometric near the initial surface by a
data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry. Here an **isometry fixing the
data** means a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying (2) (the definition is given
explicitly by these equations; no separate notion of Lorentzian isometry is
presupposed).

([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open

onto $I\times B$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) such

**(C1)** $\partial/\partial s$ is future timelike and every level set
$s^{-1}(c)$ is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that every future causal $v\in T_qM$, $q\in U$,
satisfies $|v^\sigma|\le K\,v^s$.

On the open submanifold $U$ with the induced metric and time orientation
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]), let
$$D^\pm_U(S):=\bigl\{p\in U:\ \text{every past- (respectively future-) inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\bigr\}$$
be the domains of dependence of the spacelike slice
$S:=s^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\times B$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (d), computed in

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$;

**(c)** the open set $W:=\mathrm{int}_U\bigl(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)\bigr)$

in exactly one parameter value. Consequently, $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$ is globally
hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Let $M^m$ be a smooth manifold, let $k\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $0\le k\le m$,
and let $S\subseteq M$. One says that $S$ is an **embedded $k$-dimensional
submanifold** of $M$ when for every $p\in S$ there
is a smooth chart $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with $p\in U$
such that

$$\varphi(S\cap U)=\varphi(U)\cap(\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}).$$

Such a chart is a **slice chart** for $S$ at $p$. The topology on $S$ is the
subspace topology inherited from $M$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

The next lemma proves that the restricted slice charts define a smooth
$k$-manifold structure on $S$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}$. Second covariant derivatives include their derivative-slot connection. These known background-curvature terms are zeroth order in the first-order state and vanish for the flat coordinate background. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** A map $u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
on an interval $J$ **takes values in a set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when
$u(t)(x)\in E$ for every $t\in J$ and every $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with
$u(t)$ read through its continuous representative when $s>3/2$. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$. (For $s\ge2$
the embedding clause gives a continuous representative, so the pointwise
conditions are meaningful.)

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ and let $J$ be an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$;
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, the coefficients being composed with
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$; all products are defined because
   $A^0(t,\cdot,u(t))$ and $A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lie in $H^s$ with norm bounded
   by a function of $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$, $\partial_tu(t)$ and $\partial_iu(t)$ lie
   in $H^{s-1}$, and $B(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lies in $H^s$.

**(f) Initial data.** **Initial data for $(\star)$ at time $0$** are a class
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $s\ge5$ whose values lie in a
compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for

and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth tensor fields $\Psi$, specified equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$, and a specified stress expression $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Covariance means pullback by a local diffeomorphism commutes with these equations and stress expression. Fix complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$ for this model, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$, with $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal.

The following explicit harmonic-reduction hypothesis is required. On each relatively compact initial coordinate ball, with flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, specify finite first-order variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w),$$
fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules for $w,\Psi$, and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$, shared by both solutions, such that:

**(R1)** Every smooth solution of this same model written in harmonic coordinates has extracted variables satisfying
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_iA^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
where all $A^\mu$ are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. Reconstruction recovers all matter fields and $T$ from $z$. Any internal matter gauge has already been fixed with its specified data and equations; otherwise the conclusion must include the appropriate internal gauge equivalence.
**(R2)** The initial value of $w$ is a specified smooth expression $\mathcal I(h,K,d)$ in the full data in this coordinate gauge. Thus $d$ determines every initial first-order variable, not merely initial stress tensor jets.
**(R3)** After shrinking a closed cylinder, both state ranges lie in one compact convex subset of $O$, coefficient first derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$.

These are PDE and extraction hypotheses, not an assumption of geometric uniqueness. Let $(M,g,\Psi,j)$ and $(M',g',\Psi',j')$ be two smooth time-oriented developments of this same model, solving the same Einstein equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$ and the same matter equations, whose spacelike embeddings induce $(h,K,d)$. Then near each initial point there is a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometry $\Phi$ with $\Phi\circ j=j'$ on the initial patch, $\Phi^*\Psi'=\Psi$ and consequently $\Phi^*T'=T$. Its germ along the initial patch is unique. These germs glue to one such isometry between open neighborhoods of the entire embedded initial surfaces. No uniform collar width or global-in-time assertion is made.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map and let $p\in M$. If $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ is
an isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $U$ of $p$ and $V$ of
$F(p)$ such that $F|_U:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Every open cover of a smooth manifold has a countable cover by coordinate balls with compact closures, each closure contained in one member of the original cover.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(U_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a countable cover of a smooth manifold $M$ by coordinate balls with compact closures. Then there is an at-most-countable index set $I$ and families of open sets $(W_k)_{k\in I}$ and coordinate balls $(V_k)_{k\in I}$ such that $M=\bigcup_{k\in I} W_k$, each $\overline{W_k}\subseteq V_k\subseteq \overline{V_k}\subseteq U_{n(k)}$ for some index $n(k)$, and the family $(V_k)$ is locally finite. The index set may be finite or empty.
